issues.what: T1 is the overall task copied verbatim ("The given image circulated with the following claim: ... state what could not be determined."), with no decomposition into reverse search / dating / context reading.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches the coordinator to forward the task unchanged rather than state what the workspace should establish.
issues.ideal: One task is fine here, but its text should name the steps: reverse-search E1, date the earliest matching pages, read the original caption/context, and compare with the Mecca/2023-04-12 claim.

issues.what: Rationale says Premium Times (R1) "describes a Ramadan meal at Aso Villa, contradicting the Mecca claim", but R1's visible title is only "Ramadan: Buhari hosts Tinubu to breaking of fast"; "Aso Villa" appears only in R2's (Naija Live Tv) title, and no page had been read yet.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches mixing up which source said what and treating a search snippet as a page's content before reading it.
issues.ideal: "R1 (Premium Times, titled 'Buhari hosts Tinubu to breaking of fast') has a near-identical thumbnail; get its dates to see when this copy was online."

issues.what: A date lookup on R3, an unrelated article ("Internet users on GSM networks increase to 70.3m - NCC"), justified as helping to "further refute the false claim"; its result (image first archived 2019-05-11) is never used.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches dating pages whose topic shows the image is only an incidental thumbnail, and calling the claim false before any context has been read.
issues.ideal: Skip R3, or justify it neutrally as a check on whether the unrelated page holds an earlier copy of the image.

issues.what: Rationale presumes the result: comparing E1 with E9 "will verify they are identical and confirm the original context". It also says "Presidential Villa" where E10 says "Residential Villa, Abuja". The comparison then found a 1.68% difference.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: Writing the expected outcome into the rationale teaches confirmation bias in comparisons.
issues.ideal: "Compare E1 with the Naija Live Tv image E9 to check whether it is the same photograph and whether anything was altered."

issues.what: The E7 'review comparison image' step is justified as "Reading E24 will provide the formal tool result to cite", not as looking at the diff composite to check the match.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches that reviewing a comparison is about collecting citations rather than checking the picture.
issues.ideal: "View the E24 composite to confirm visually that E1 and the Premium Times thumbnail E5 are the same photograph before reporting."

issues.what: The verifier fed back "wrong_citation/critical", but the REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word identical to the original ANSWER.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: If the flag was valid, the exported answer still carries the bad citation; if it was not, the no-op revise step is noise in the training data.
issues.ideal: The revise step should either change the flagged citation or the pipeline should record why it was rejected.

good_patterns: Standard provenance chain done in order: OCR, reverse image search, dates for the top matches, reading the earliest dated page's text, then pixel comparisons of E1 against both matching copies (E9 and E5).

Careful date semantics in the report and answer: "no later than May 10, 2019 according to the page's declared publication date", and the archive capture "establishes the page's existence by that date, not its first publication date".

Honest comparison reporting: the 0.000% match with the thumbnail is hedged ("thresholded comparison of a small thumbnail"), and the 1.68% difference with the Naija Live TV copy is reported rather than hidden.

Attribution is kept: "the Abuja context comes from the accompanying report" / "room's location was not independently established", and the report scopes what is false (the image's context) without claiming the two men never met in Mecca.
cannot_judge: The rest of E10 is truncated (+1580 chars), so I could not check the 'Friday evening' detail or whether the page gives an event date beyond the publication date.
Whether the watermark in F6 ("visibly carries a large watermark across this region") is actually visible in E9/E21; the images are attached but not rendered here, and no review step looked at E21.
Which citation the verifier flagged as wrong_citation/critical; none of the visible citations looks clearly wrong to me.
summary: A short, well-ordered E-family run: reverse search found 2019 Naija Live TV and Premium Times copies; dates, page text and two pixel comparisons support an honestly hedged conclusion that the image is a May 2019 Abuja Ramadan-meal photo, not Mecca 2023. The issues are minor: a verbatim GIA task, rationales that mix up sources or presume outcomes, one wasted date lookup on an unrelated page, and a no-op answer revision after a critical verifier flag. Nothing here would teach hallucination or wrong verdicts.
